text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has directed the Sindh provincial chief minister to find a political solution to end lawlessness in Karachi.
- Five people were killed in two shooting incidents in Lahore, the capital of Punjab province. Four victims were shot dead while offering prayers at a mosque.
- The government has decided to adjust consumer prices for oil products and lubricants on a yearly rather than a monthly basis, as has been the practice since January 1, 1996.
- Liquid foreign reserves rose $11 million to $1.026 billion on June 21, the State (central) Bank of Pakistan said.
- The Defence Ministry may open domestic routes to foreign airlines, sources in the state's Civil Aviation Authority said.
- A man shot dead 10 people, including eight members of his family, over a petty dispute in Hussain Kot, Azad Kashmir.
- Senate (upper house) to meet after a weekly two-day recess.
- Opposition Leader Benazir Bhutto has called for formation of a national government to take the country out of crisis.
